SEARCH
Package com.bilt.pos.media.service

Interface AdDecisionService

All Known Implementing Classes:
InMemoryAdDecisionService
public interface AdDecisionService
The ad platform as the retail-media widget sees it: register a session, ask for decisions, validate taps, report interactions, listen for platform-originated events.

Provisional. This contract is defined ahead of the platform integration spec so the widget, surfaces and emulator can be built against it; it will be revised when that spec lands and the platform-backed implementation follows in RET-6784. Until then the only implementation is InMemoryAdDecisionService. Method shapes may change; the principle that the service never sees checkout session types (only AdSessionSnapshot) will not.

Timeouts and failures

The register's checkout must never wait on advertising. Every method is bounded:

  • registerSession(com.bilt.pos.media.service.AdSessionSnapshot) and updateSession(com.bilt.pos.media.service.SessionHandle, com.bilt.pos.media.service.AdSessionSnapshot) return promptly. An implementation that talks to a network does so asynchronously behind the handle; registration never blocks on the platform, and a register that is slow or down manifests as decisions coming back empty, not as a stalled checkout.
  • decide(com.bilt.pos.media.service.SessionHandle, com.bilt.pos.media.Placement, com.bilt.pos.media.Capabilities, java.time.Duration) returns within the caller's timeout or answers Optional.empty(). A miss — no fill, a slow platform, a network failure, an unsupported creative — is an empty answer, never an exception. Only programming errors (a null argument, a handle that was never issued) throw.
  • validateAction(com.bilt.pos.media.service.SessionHandle, com.bilt.pos.widget.Cta, java.lang.String) answers ActionOutcome.rejected(java.lang.String) rather than throwing when the platform refuses or cannot be reached; an unreachable platform means the offer is not applied, which is the safe default.
  • report(com.bilt.pos.media.service.SessionHandle, com.bilt.pos.media.AdInteraction) is fire-and-forget; implementations buffer and retry internally and drop on the floor before they block the caller.
  • subscribe(com.bilt.pos.media.service.SessionHandle, com.bilt.pos.media.service.AdEventListener) delivers on a service-owned thread and tolerates a listener that is slow; a listener that throws is logged and dropped from that delivery only.

Implementations are thread-safe; the widget calls them from its executor and the surfaces' callback threads.

  • Method Details

    • registerSession

      SessionHandle registerSession(AdSessionSnapshot snapshot)
      Announces a shopper session and returns the handle every later call uses. Returns promptly without waiting on the platform.

    • updateSession

      void updateSession(SessionHandle handle, AdSessionSnapshot snapshot)
      Replaces the service's view of the session with snapshot. The whole snapshot is sent each time; the service diffs against what it has if it wants to. Returns promptly.

    • decide

      Optional<Rendering> decide(SessionHandle handle, Placement placement, Capabilities capabilities, Duration timeout)
      Asks for a creative to show in placement, given what the register can render. Returns within timeout either a rendering the platform decided on and the capabilities allow, or empty for any kind of miss. Never throws for a miss.

    • validateAction

      ActionOutcome validateAction(SessionHandle handle, Cta cta, String creativeId)
      Presents a tapped cta for creativeId to the platform. The answer is accepted with an Offer for an APPLY_OFFER, accepted without one for the other actions, or rejected with a diagnostic reason when the token is unknown, already used, expired, or belongs to a different creative or session.

    • report

      void report(SessionHandle handle, AdInteraction interaction)
      Reports one interaction for measurement. Fire-and-forget; never blocks the caller.

    • subscribe

      AdEventSubscription subscribe(SessionHandle handle, AdEventListener listener)
      Opens the server-to-SDK event channel for handle: offers and interactions that originate outside the SDK's own renderer (a hosted page, a send-to-phone confirmation). Close the returned subscription to stop delivery; closeSession(com.bilt.pos.media.service.SessionHandle) closes it too.

    • closeSession

      void closeSession(SessionHandle handle)
      Ends the session on the service side: outstanding tokens stop validating, subscriptions are closed, and the handle is no longer accepted. Idempotent.
